title: Lemon Caper Chicken

items.raw: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ pounds)
1 teaspoon kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper
¼ cup fresh lemon juice (about 2 lemons)

steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally into two thin pieces. Pound between plastic wrap to an even ¼-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper and dredge lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the cutlets in batches 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F). Move to a warm plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, and cook 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; simmer until reduced by half.
Add the stock, lemon juice, and capers and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Off the heat, swirl in the remaining 3 tablespoons of cold butter until the sauce is glossy. Taste for salt and lemon.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, turn to coat, and scatter with parsley.

notes.label: Even thickness
notes.text: pounding the cutlets evenly is what lets them cook in minutes without drying out.

notes.label: No wine
notes.text: use an extra ½ cup stock and a teaspoon more lemon juice.

notes.label: Alongside
notes.text: buttered linguine, rice, or the roasted halved tomatoes from Chapter 9.
